author: d. w. myers
title: Senator Collins highlights Essential Air Service and air traffic controller staffing at budget hearing
text:
Senator Susan Collins, Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, stressed the importance of the Essential Air Service program in Maine and raised concerns about air traffic controller shortages during a Department of Transportation budget hearing on May 20.
The discussion focused on how federal funding decisions impact rural communities’ access to commercial air service and efforts to modernize the nation’s airspace system. The Senate Appropriations Committee manages legislation related to federal funding, conducts hearings on spending proposals, and oversees government programs, according to the official website .
Collins said, “The Essential Air Service program is truly a lifeline to rural communities across the country, helping to connect them to national and global transportation networks, as well as to critical services, such as health care.” She emphasized that four airports in Maine—Presque Isle, Rockland, Augusta, and Trenton—depend on this program for commercial air service. Expressing concern over proposed cuts in the President’s budget for this program, Collins asked Secretary Sean Duffy how he would support rural air service if such reductions occur.
Duffy responded by affirming his understanding of Essential Air Service’s value: “As you know…I understand how important Essential Air Service is for communities who normally do not get service but for this program…this Administration found resources to maintain service to rural communities…funding Essential Air Service when the government was shut down. So I think that does underscore the commitment to the communities that are served by this great program.” He added that while seeking efficiencies is part of their approach, they do not want any community cut off from air travel.
Collins also commended Duffy for efforts in modernizing airspace systems but pointed out severe staffing shortages at airports like Bangor. She asked about providing bonuses or financial incentives for controllers willing to relocate or start work at understaffed locations. Duffy replied: “This is a broader conversation…Sometimes folks want to go to Bangor…there’s an issue…our cost of living for controllers and how much we can pay them…So maybe that’s a conversation we could have together because it’s gotten expensive in America.” He agreed with Collins’s suggestion about considering financial incentives and committed: “I’ll do some research on it. Thank you Senator.”
The Senate Appropriations Committee oversees federal expenditures as mandated by law under authority from the U.S. Constitution; it has influenced federal spending through its oversight role since its early operations—including chairmanships like Lot Morrill of Maine—and produces appropriations bills such as those funding homeland security programs according to its official website .
Looking ahead, both Collins and Duffy indicated willingness for continued collaboration on these issues as Congress prepares future appropriations bills affecting transportation infrastructure.
